abstract: Generalized Laguerre expressions of the completed Riemann xi-function characterize the reality of its zeros through inequalities at every order and height. For every fixed $c_0>1/2$, we prove positivity at every sufficiently large height $t$ for all orders $2p\ge c_0\log(t/(2\pi))$, with no upper restriction on $p$. An exact zero-product comparison makes the entire coefficient tail positive above $O(\log^2t)$, and a saddle estimate uniform through powers of the logarithm covers the remaining range. At typical heights, xi positivity holds simultaneously at all orders $2p\ge N(T)$ for every $N(T)\to\infty$. For both Hardy's function and normalized xi, we prove vanishing relative error against $2|\zeta(1/2+n/\log T+it)|^2$ simultaneously for even $N(T)\le n\le b\log T$. This approximation uses logarithmic zeta ratios, subharmonic bounds, and classical zero density on dyadic order blocks; its range is not extended to arbitrary orders. We also prove a coefficient-uniform positive arithmetic mean on intervals of length $H=T^\nu$. At order $n\sim\alpha\log T$, $0<\alpha<1/2$, arbitrary complex Dirichlet-polynomial filters of length $T^\theta$ are permitted when $\theta<\nu-\rho(\alpha)$, where $\rho(\alpha)=1/2-\alpha+\alpha\log(2\alpha)$. The full-height length exponent approaches one as the fixed order ratio approaches one half. Grouping integer frequencies and a common diagonal Mellin contour retain the complete coefficient norm. A fixed-shift Bettin–Chandee–Radziwiłł argument gives a complementary cancellation range at small order ratios. Finite CPU identity controls accompany the proofs. The matching pointwise bounds still prevent direct concentration on bounded negative sets in the arithmetic range. Classical zero density is used, not improved. Small fixed orders, exceptional zero ordinates, and the Riemann hypothesis remain unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Adds Theorem1a and Sections4.2–4.4: every Xi Laguerre order above a fixed logarithmic threshold is positive at each sufficiently large height, without an upper cutoff. A coefficientwise derivative inequality for the far-zero product gives an entire positive tail, and a uniform polylogarithmic saddle estimate supplies the overlap. Adds Theorem4, Section10, and Corollary4a: relative approximation on every range N(T)<=n<=b logT, a quantitative common exceptional set, a classical Gaussian corollary, and simultaneous Xi positivity at all diverging orders without an upper cutoff. Extends Theorem2 to short intervals and polynomial filters with theta<nu-rho(alpha), retaining arbitrary coefficient norms by integer-frequency grouping and a common diagonal contour. Adds Theorem2a and Section7.6 for the complementary fixed-shift BCR cancellation range, with complete coefficient norms, both Poisson-mode terms, zero-mode contour, and endpoints. Expands the scalar-source contour and convergence details in response to the v2 review. The concentration limitation uses the matching pointwise envelope and classical subconvexity; the inverse-gcd bound is the subpower estimate actually proved in Lemma5. Updates the abstract, related work, acknowledgments, quantifiers, and limitations. Adds exact coefficient-tail, paired-gamma, convolution-norm, and residue controls and the dyadic-disk illustration. No RH, unfiltered moment, or zero-density improvement is claimed.
title: Generalized Laguerre positivity at growing orders
